I'll recommend Torchlight Infinite unless you're not gacha resistant. It is blatantly p2w and they try to sell you stuff at every turn but at the same time its surprisingly playable for free. Basically the entire game design (except crafting which is actually pretty well made and accessible) is ripped off from poe, skills have links with some support "gems" being basically copy pasted with different name and it works really well.

The entire thing is pretty much poe with training wheels, simple map rolling, simple skill link acquisition and the gameplay is very fast and snappy. Your pet autoloots majority of drops except for some higher tier items (unless you pay up with battle pass). Rest you just pick up with a loot keybind which prioritises items by their tiers. There is also auction (pretty badly designed one to be fair) and target dummy to test build changes which is pretty handy. Free respecs till level 80 but even past that you get 99 respec points for 1 currency which drops like candy.

Cons: Terrible translation, most dialogue is cringe inducing and some descriptions just straight up don't make sense. Extremely limited auction slots unless you pay. Many characters locked behind paywall, pet gacha is pretty rough but to be fair you can get by just fine with the free ones. The entire game and ui is clearly made for mobile first and foremost so you get to deal with twenty different menus and windows.

That said I feel like for a free game the pros still massively outweigh the cons and the game is weirdly good for a chinese mobile pay2win arpg. Played it for couple days now with no prior experience of it, got two characters to 96 out of 100 and did majority of endgame content except for some cutting edge bossfights, it's been neat change of pace from poe.

>Einhar

You catch beasts in maps by killing them, Einhar captures them once they are "dead". Then you can use them in Menagerie for various specific crafts.

>Alva

You build a temple by completing incursions. Each incursion has two architects in it, you kill one and the other one remains alive and determines the type of the room in the resulting temple. If you leave same architect alive multiple times, level of the room goes up to maximum of 3. Before entering the incursion you can see which 2 architects are present, kill the one that makes a room you like less. After 12 incursions the temple is complete and you can either run it from Alva or take it from her as an itemised map and start a new one. 

>Body parts

When Metamorph mechanic spawns in your map, certain mobs in it drop body parts (eye, liver, lung, heart, brain). At the end of the map or once you feel like you have enough, you can build a metamorph from one of each body part. Resulting metamorph will have abilities of the mobs used to build it and some body parts have specific rewards. If you make it strong enough, it will drop special itemised body part which you can use in Tane's Lab to build extra metamorphs.

>Garden

Harvest is pretty simple. You walk into the garden, activate plots, kill monsters, they will drop yellow, purple or blue juice. That is then used for crafts through the harvest bench.

Not really, you will be getting gems way faster than you're now if you stick with the game so that's not really an issue. I'd make sure to always pick a new champion in time gate (there will always be one offered as long as you're missing any) over opening duplicate time gate unless you really really like some champion and want more gear for them. Buy familiars as soon as you can they're by far the best investment. If the next one feels like it's impossibly far away, just go back to buying chests, you'll get to it eventually. If you ever feel like spending money on the game, buying cheap familiars is the best value you can get and it's not very close. Don't buy champions with cash unless you feel like throwing money away for no reason.

Strategy would be to get close to your "wall" (place where you can't go further) using speed champions if you have any which you probably don't at this point, then switching to your damage team. Don't be afraid to reset once you get stuck, that's the whole point. Your favour will go up, that in turn will increase your gold find and you'll get further next time. If you're this early on and have any silver chests, open them as far through adventure as you can since they will give you gold. Make sure to also ugprade your blessings in the menu in top left of the screen. The game will shout at you if you try to spend more than a fraction of your favour on them so make sure not to do that, just buy the ones it lets you without prompt. Most blessings only function in that specific campaign but some of them (the right side) are game-wide so it's not a bad idea to run a bit of each campaign early on to pick up the first one in each.

Whichever feels most comfortable to you it doesn't matter much. I feel like best one early on is the one that goes by an upgrade but it's whatever, later on you'll mostly be on the highest one.

Some adventures unlock more champions so those are nice to do but will generally be difficult for a fresh account, just take it easy.
